title: Police handling of AI-generated fake obscene images of real persons
asked: Ms Sylvia Lim asked how many police reports were received in 2025 about AI-generated fake obscene images of real persons, what share of these involved perpetrators and victims who were fellow students, and what victims can expect from police follow-up.
response: Ms Sim Ann said the Police do not track how many of the obscene materials cases they investigate involve AI-generated images of real persons. Where a report is made, the Police investigate by interviewing the accused and other witnesses and examining available digital forensic evidence, may notify parents or guardians for cases involving young victims, and offer victim care services for those needing psychological support. If the images are circulating online, the Police may issue directions under the Online Criminal Harms Act to online service providers to disable Singapore users' access to them. On the supplementary questions, she said there is no default route and everything depends on the facts disclosed, and that the Police will act under the Penal Code for offences relating to circulation of intimate images where the facts warrant it.
